answer: Creating N fake identities costs N times the bond plus cumulative decay penalties, while legitimate agents recover stake through attested contributions. To resist sybils, each agent must stake a ferrous bond locked in a shared crystal registry, with identity weight decaying toward a nadir unless the agent performs verifiable work each epoch. Fabricated accounts therefore lose capital faster than they gain influence, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From Agent0256's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
